paraphrase: Śiva tells Pārvatī of his descent between the Dvāpara and Kali ages: in the line of the sage Atri the brahmin Viśvarūpa and his devoted wife Sudarśanā lived at Ulkāgrāma; Śiva was conceived and born to her on the fourteenth of the bright half of Caitra, a tawny-eyed, golden child, and the birth rites were performed.
speaker: Śiva (Īśvara)
notes: Checked against the Muktabodha e-text M00508 of the Ganakarika with Ratnatika (C. D. Dalal ed., GOS 15, Baroda 1920) in sources_raw.

paraphrase: The infant was found each day to have performed the fire-offering; when his parents watched and questioned him he fainted and died at seven months; his mother laid him in the sacred pool, and Śiva, having stilled the body, entered it; the child was seen playing in the water, and the sages praised him as Mahādeva in the form of a child.
speaker: Śiva (Īśvara)
notes: Checked against the Muktabodha e-text M00508 of the Ganakarika with Ratnatika (C. D. Dalal ed., GOS 15, Baroda 1920) in sources_raw.

paraphrase: Lakulīśa came to Kāyāvarohaṇa in the Bhṛgu region and merged into the Brahmeśvara liṅga; because the Lord descended there in bodily form the place is called Kāyāvarohaṇa. His image holds a club in the left hand and a citron in the right. The tīrtha was called Icchāpurī in the Kṛta age, Māyāpurī in the Tretā, Meghavatī in the Dvāpara and Kāyāvarohaṇa in the Kali; in the terrible Kali age the Lord is known as Lakulīśa, for the liberation of beings.
speaker: Śiva (Īśvara)
notes: Checked against the Muktabodha e-text M00508 of the Ganakarika with Ratnatika (C. D. Dalal ed., GOS 15, Baroda 1920) in sources_raw.
